questions.q: What is packet rate in ELRS?
questions.explain: More packets mean lower latency, but worse sensitivity and range.

questions.q: For a long-range wing over forest, the better choice is…
questions.explain: The long wavelength diffracts around obstacles, and a low packet rate gives sensitivity margin.

questions.q: Telem ratio 1:128 at 500 Hz gives telemetry once every…

options: The basis of the hopping pattern
A password that encrypts the control link
questions.explain: It is not a secret and not protection: a unique phrase keeps you from coinciding with neighbors. A phrase alone is not enough: the ELRS major versions on the module and the receiver must match too.

questions.q: LQ at 100% with RSSI at the sensitivity threshold means…
options: All is well: every packet gets through
The edge of the link with no margin
questions.explain: LQ says whether packets get through, RSSI how much margin is left. You need both.

questions.q: RXLOSS when turning with your back to the pilot. The likely cause?
options: The antenna is shadowed by the frame
A low packet rate and a weak radio battery
Interference from the 5.8 GHz video transmitter
questions.explain: A shadowed antenna is the classic. Move it out and orient it.
50 Hz is −115, 500 Hz is −105. The LoRa mode thresholds in ELRS 4.1 are the same as in 3.x (the `common.cpp` table).

questions.q: Telemetry ratio 1:128 at 250 Hz gives a telemetry interval of:
A long-range flight, ELRS 2.4 GHz in 250 Hz mode. Telemetry at the edge of the area:
questions.fragment:
RSSI1 -104 dBm  RSSI2 -106 dBm  LQ 71%  SNR -2 dB
mode sensitivity 250 Hz ≈ -108 dBm
options: A 2–4 dB margin is a link on the verge of failsafe: lower the packet rate or turn back
LQ 71 % is normal for long range; failsafe only comes below LQ 10 %
SNR -2 dB means a faulty receiver: a healthy one is always positive
Raise the packet rate to 500 Hz: that improves receiver sensitivity
questions.explain: The margin is counted from the mode's sensitivity; 500 Hz is even less sensitive.

questions.q: The radio module was updated to ELRS 4.1, the receiver stayed on 3.6 with the same binding phrase. What happens?
options: They will not link by any binding method
They link after three receiver power-ups
questions.explain: `OTA_VERSION_ID` (3 → 4) is mixed into the CRC and the hopping sequence: 3.x and 4.x do not sync. Both sides have to be updated.

questions.q: A whoop with a built-in SPI ELRS receiver on Betaflight 2025.12 and a module on ELRS 4.1. A working option?
options: Flash the whoop's receiver to 4.1 with ExpressLRS Configurator
A separate ELRS 4.x serial receiver on a UART, or a 3.x module for this model
questions.explain: The SPI receiver runs Betaflight's code; in 2025.12 that is ELRS 3 (`ELRS_OTA_VERSION_ID 3`). ELRS 4 support for SPI comes in Betaflight 2026.6 with the `ELRSV4` build.

questions.q: What must you save before updating a device from ELRS 3.x to 4.x?
options: The binding phrase: it gets erased
`hardware.json` and the Options settings from the Web UI
Nothing: the update happens in place
questions.explain: The file system changes from SPIFFS to LittleFS, and custom `hardware.json` and `options.json` are erased. `elrsV3.lua`, on the contrary, is deleted and replaced with `elrs.lua`.
